source_text: De Christo et ecclesia: vulpes perversi doctores haereticorum, qui argumentorum calliditate vineam Domini exterminant. Doctores ecclesiae potestatem capiendi vulpes accipiunt, sicut calcandi serpentes. Pusillae vineae — animae rudes — laedi possunt; perfectae non facile scandalizantur. Capite nobis: mihi sponso et sponsae, vel mihi et sodalibus.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning Christ and church: foxes perverse teachers of-heretics, who by-arguments' cleverness vineyard of-Lord destroy. Teachers of-church power of-catching foxes receive, as of-trampling serpents. Little vineyards — souls raw — to-be-hurt are-able; perfect not easily are-scandalized. Catch for-us: to-me bridegroom and to-bride, or to-me and to-companions.
pass_b_english: Of Christ and the church: the foxes are perverse teachers of heresies, who by clever arguments spoil the Lord’s vineyard. Teachers of the church receive power to catch foxes, as to tread on serpents. Little vineyards — unformed souls — can be hurt; the perfect are not easily scandalized. Catch for us: for me the Bridegroom and for the Bride, or for me and my companions.
